register.name: NSW Fair Trading Complaints Register
register.threshold: Businesses (including online businesses) that received 10 or more complaints in a calendar month
register.format: Interactive Power BI dashboard only (embedded on the page). No CSV/JSON/XLSX download and no dataset on data.nsw.gov.au (CKAN API searches for the register returned nothing).
register.workerNote: Not a plain file URL. Power BI 'publish to web' renders client-side via an undocumented API; scraping it is fragile and not an official data feed. Link out or embed the official dashboard instead.
register.notPublished: Outcomes, penalties or details of specific complaints; anonymous complaints are excluded (a complaint needs a name and at least one contact method)
register.updateFrequency: Monthly, published in the second half of each month, covering complaints received in the previous calendar month
register.latestMonthExpected: September 2026 (published second half of October 2026); the page itself does not state the month shown, so confirm in the dashboard
register.disclaimer: No verbatim disclaimer is shown on the register page. Suggested wording based on official statements: 'The register shows businesses with 10 or more complaints lodged with NSW Fair Trading in a month. A listing is a count of complaints, not a finding of wrongdoing. Each complaint is assessed and NSW Fair Trading considers the trader's conduct before deciding whether action is needed. Source: NSW Fair Trading Complaints Register.'

accc.note: The ACCC does not publish a 'most complained about businesses' list or complaints data by business.

report.detail: If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 000.
Call your bank or card provider immediately to report the scam and ask them to stop any transactions. Use the number on your card or the bank's official app/website.
report.phone: CommBank 13 2221 | Westpac 1300 364 294 | NAB 13 22 65 | ANZ cards 13 22 73, internet banking 13 33 50
report.srcName: Scamwatch; bank pages: commbank.com.au/support/security.html, westpac.com.au/security/how-to-report/, nab.com.au/about-us/security/report-fraud-scams, anz.com.au/security/report-scams-fraud/

report.step: Get free recovery help from IDCARE
report.detail: IDCARE is the national identity and cyber support service. It helps you make a free plan to limit the damage (Mon-Fri 7am-7pm AEST). NSW/ACT direct line 02 8999 3356.

report.step: Report cybercrime or money lost to police (ReportCyber)
report.detail: Make an official online report to police through ReportCyber, run by the Australian Cyber Security Centre. Advice line: Australian Cyber Security Hotline.

NSW Police directs fraud and cybercrime reports to ReportCyber. For non-urgent police help call the Police Assistance Line; you can also attend a police station with a completed Fraud Report Form. Share information anonymously with Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000.
Report the scam to Scamwatch (National Anti-Scam Centre) to help warn others and disrupt scammers. Scam websites have their own form: https://forms.scamwatch.gov.au/report-a-scamwebsite/

report.step: Not happy with your bank's response?
report.detail: Complain to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA), a free, independent service.
Scammers often come back to past victims, especially offering to 'help you get your money back'. Change passwords on your devices and accounts.
Scams are stressful. Free, confidential support is available 24/7 from Lifeline (13 11 14) and Beyond Blue (1300 22 4636), and free financial counselling via Moneysmart.

report.step: Complaint about a NSW business (not a scam)
report.detail: For a dispute with a legitimate business, contact NSW Fair Trading.

tips.detail: Stop: take a moment before giving money or personal info to anyone. Check: make sure the person or organisation is real. Protect: act quickly if something feels wrong.

tips.tip: Never share one-time codes, PINs or passwords
tips.detail: No real bank or agency will ask for your passwords, PINs, NetCode/security codes or one-time passcodes. Anyone who does is a scammer.

tips.tip: There is no such thing as a 'safe account'
tips.detail: Your bank will never ask you to move money to another account to keep it safe. That account belongs to the scammer.

tips.tip: Hang up and call back on a number you find yourself
tips.detail: If a call feels off, hang up. Call the organisation back using the number on your card or its official website or app, never the number the caller gives you.

tips.tip: Caller ID and SMS names can be faked
tips.detail: Scammers can make a call or text look like it is from your bank's real number, even in the same message thread. A familiar number proves nothing.

tips.tip: Don't tap links in unexpected texts or emails
tips.detail: Log in by typing the bank's address yourself or using its official app. Banks won't ask you to log on via a link in an SMS or email.

tips.tip: Never let a caller onto your device
tips.detail: Don't download software, share your screen or give remote access to someone who contacts you. Banks and government agencies won't ask.
Scammers rush you so you don't spot the warning signs. Don't let anyone hurry you into paying or sharing details - a genuine organisation will wait.

tips.tip: Be wary of odd ways to pay
tips.detail: Requests to pay by gift cards, cash withdrawals, crypto or crypto ATMs are classic scam signs. CommBank will never ask you to withdraw cash or buy gift cards.

tips.tip: Big returns, no risk? It's a scam
tips.detail: Check any adviser holds an Australian financial services (AFS) licence with ASIC and isn't on the Moneysmart investor alert list before investing.
